slides.title: 95% of all Bitcoin is already mined.
slides.sub: So who gets the last 896,000 coins, and when?

slides.title: Mined so far
paras: Bitcoin's supply is capped at <u>21 million</u>. About <g>20.10 million</g> already exist.
That leaves roughly <r>896,000</r> coins still to be mined.
slides.source: Hotcoin calc. from block height 973,309 (mempool.space); blockchain.info total: 20,104,053 BTC

slides.title: Half as much every 4 years
paras: Every 210,000 blocks (about 4 years), the reward for mining a block <u>halves</u>.
Half of all Bitcoin came out in the first era alone.
slides.source: Bitcoin issuance schedule: 210,000 blocks per era, reward halves each era

slides.title: The next halving
paras: The next one comes at <u>block 1,050,000</u>, about 76,700 blocks from now.
At ~144 blocks a day, that's around <g>April 2028</g>. The reward drops to 1.5625 BTC.
slides.source: mempool.space block height, Oct 27, 2026; date assumes 10-minute blocks

slides.title: 450 new coins a day
paras: 144 blocks × 3.125 BTC = <u>about 450 new bitcoin per day</u>.
At ~$80K that's roughly <g>$36M</g> a day of new supply. Spot Bitcoin ETFs can move 10x that in a single session.

visual.title: New BTC per day, by era

slides.source: Hotcoin calc.: 144 blocks/day × reward at each halving

slides.title: The last coin
paras: Halvings keep shrinking the reward, so the final fractions of a bitcoin are mined around <u>the year 2140</u>.
After that, miners are paid only by transaction fees.
slides.source: Hotcoin calc. from the issuance schedule. Not financial advice.
